author: 🇦🇹 roflstoffl
content:
#sticky pls:
Basic ideal Single Target Rotation for Leveling as Melee (1h + Shield or 2h)

-) Lightning Shield on
-) Run towards the Mob
-) Pull with Flame Shock
-) Auto Attack till Death

MultiMob (or one mob  after another)
-) Drop Searing Totem
-) if mana allows drop agility and/or stoneskin or strength
-) drop Nova/Magma Totem
-)Auto Attack

WF/Rockbiter/Flametongue/Frostbrand doesnt matter.
No significant difference in dps outcome.

I save money and just buy Rockbiter for consistent dps increase.

In general, when you wear +spell gear or when you fight high armored mobs ~> use Flametongue/Frostbrand

Ofc there are other strategies,
Like for multi mobs: Stoneclaw first and pick them 1on1, … but they have more downtime in the long run

(Source: Melderon)

author: August 🇲🇰
content:
tons of combos you can make with warstomp, warstomp into iron grenade (guranteed 4 seconds aoe stun), warstomp + heal, warstomp for cast interrupt, warstomp for kiting to gain distance, warstomp chainlightning+shock combo, warstomp fire nova totem and so on, so many uses in so many situations. basically you use it all the time, as one of your regular abilities and it got quite a low cd.

Warstomp into iron grenade combo i used all the time, to say short its op. even if multiple melees is on you, you can get away. stunning them all for 4 seconds while walking away, then droping earthbind and continue kiting. cant imagine playing without it. dunno what orcs do, when few melees is on them.

plus you get +200 hp, and health is one of the main stats in pvp, how many times you survive at 5% hp and win a fight? - a ton. as an orc you would be dead.

Orc is rng, and only "works" against stun classes, there arent really a ton of stuns in vanilla, which is mostly rogues, warriors, paladins + (druids bash, mage fireblast). Against other classes, spells and situations you have no racial, as an orc, when taurens 200+ hp is constantly valuable against all classes and situations.

And as you said orc stun resist is rng, tons of times it will work, when its irrelevant and makes no difference, and when you need it - it doesnt work, in that key moment you need. its unreliable, only one out of 4 stuns it'll do the trick. Yea resisting stun is fine and you maybe win fight because of it from time to time, but it feels cheap, you know that next 3 times you wont resist it, and you will lose.

basically that is my thoughts and experience. One more plus for orcs is that they got a smaller size model, so you may stay unnoticed and will be less targeted in bgs.

author: Thraxeus
content:
Ah I detest crit compilation videos I never watch them. But honestly I actually rate enh shamans in pvp. Especially when they play defensively and focus on their strength of attrition to exhaust an opponents resources or cds then go in with burst damage to close the fight.

Mail and shield makes them very solid V phys dps (sans paladins but thats a whole other can of fucking twow worms) Combined with multiple slow options means they can outpace most of them well.

Totem options for prettymuch every situation gives them an incredible toolkit that's often overlooked.
Proper grounding totem usage for absorbing high-impact spells and a ranged 6sec cd silence that's dirt cheap makes them very good versus casters and allows them to often times trade very well with mana economy until the other player has exhausted their options.
likewise purge being very very strong just in and of itself. 

5% hitcap in pvp means with 3% on gear they only need 2/2 from gear  to make everything hit which is very easy to get imo.

(pvp stuff over)


Id agree that uptime buffs could be an option for increasing their PvE dps as you usually have very limited uptime in PVP situations so could be good. But the question is how would you want to increase that damage?
If it's a damage boost people will try and get as fast a 2h as possible (MCP again)
If it's a speed boost then you fall into the problem of WF having an ICD which fucks so many things.(this would be a change that I would 100% get behind WF for shamans should have no internal CD and be able to proc off itself)

author: 𝓶𝓮𝓮𝓫𝔂𝓫𝓫
content:
My personal preference would probably be this. With 10-20, it's up to you whether u go 5/5 concussion over 2/2 earth's grasp or not - for me, making earthbind and stoneclaw more useful is good for survivability while levelling. With 20-40, its up to u whether u take imp gw before 5/5 thundering strikes or not. just makes it easier to get around and escape danger. with 40-60, you can opt to spec into resto a bit, because you will likely use healing wave between mobs - just cuts down on time spent recovering. not to mention it can come in handy if you want to heal a dungeon every now and then. Also its kinda unnecessary to use stormstrike while levelling and elemental weapons is a miniscule damage increase, if it even works. someone else confirm whether or not it does. the build doesnt include bloodlust either because, well, you will likely respec at 60 anyway. the shield talents are very useful in a pinch, you will definitely want to set up a 1h+shield macro even if you prefer a 2h big bonk to level up. increasing survivability is crucial for shaman levelling imo, since we dont do well when pulling extra mobs unless we pull out a shield. you can really shuffle around points how you want, but i would say the points in enh and ele are the essential ones.

author: Papairoh
content: If the player youre trying to kill has some nr, it will be most likely be bis. Spell pen that actually does its thing is by far more impactful than any other stat. It varies in effectiveness but as long as they have close to 20 resistance it will be very strong. At 20 resistance youre looking at a 5.2% damage increase. This would equate to like 75 sp in bis ele builds. If they had an nr set on for some reason, maybe sitting at like 200 nr, it would double in value, giving you a 10% damage increase or roughly 140 sp. In pvp crit is valued higher and stam is valued high so even compared to the typical bis option for pen rings in raid (the ring of prophet skeram) don rodriogo's band is quite good. If you know for sure though that your opponenet doesnt have resistances then dont bother. But druids for example always will unless you purge them cause motw

author: Vigrid
content:
Hey folks, I've been abusing this a while but I'm happy to let the cat out of the bag.

8/8 T1 for Resto Shaman is broken and I daresay actually BiS right now. The bounces behave no different to regular Healing Wave  for the purposes of Primal Surge, but Undertow can be procced multiple times on a single cast assuming the waves bounce. This means if you have max stacks of Water Shield, it can proc one for mana, restore a charge, and proc it again. 5/8 already acted favourably with these bounces and could independently proc as well, but these two extra talents basically means we can spam max rank Healing Wave bombs for entire fights, which is ridiculous. I've included some logs to showcase the insanity here on Faerlina, Patchwerk, and Thaddius P2 because they're the consistently highest damage fights in the game (and I basically had to move every single Polarity Shift on Thadd so I could have done much better). Priest in second place is abusing 8/8 T2 which is broken in its own right, and the Shaman/Priest below us are just using more general goodstuff healing builds. The only real weakness or shortcoming of this build is that your mana economy isn't insane if the Waves are simply not bouncing at all because they're either no targets around your initial target or they're all 100% HP.

author: Vigrid
content:
It's still good nothing has really changed. The drop off can be significant when the raid damage is a super even distribution because the bounces underheal and the primary target overheals but it's usually not too serious. 

The only fight I feel a strong need to use Chain Heal is KT for melee Frost Blast because those harder hitting bounces are needed to actually save melee.

author: Vigrid
content: A side benefit is that because all bounces have 100% chance to apply Healing Way unlike Chain Heal, you have about thrice the proc economy of Healing Way and are actually boosting the performance of other Rshams in the raid.

author: Vigrid
content:
The problem with Enh threat is that they have non-normalized weapon damage on Stormstrike and Lightningstrike, so slow weapons are crazy good. So they swing some 3.8 nonsense which is inherently a super high variance weapon, and then they combine the super high variance weapon with the super high variance Windfury Imbue and their threat profile looks like a rollercoaster on the fritz. Calming Winds is just a weaker modifier than Cat/Battle/Berserker/Being a Rogue (0.85 vs 0.8) also shocks are completely uncovered by Calming Winds and do full threat so Enhance total threat is just silly high relative to the damage they deal.

I propose to rework the Windfury effect of the Elemental Weapons talent to specifically give you dramatically lower threat on Windfury attacks. That should both lower their total threat and reduce the "WTFOMGBBQ 6K THREAT ONE AUTO" nonsense going on.

- Has anyone tried a small, tight group for BRD Arena (for chest piece, the spell hit gear from that too) for less gear competition, and if so, what was the group you were using? (I was considering doing it 2-3 man, pocket heals and some dps that can take some punishment).

Anyways, long post I realize, but I’m just looking for something interesting content-wise instead of “Do lashers or farm for Dark Runes.”

I realize I’ll have to farm for Dark Runes no matter what (but even for those, I was looking into alternative farms for them, such as the Fel Guards in Blasted Lands instead of the typical Satyrs in Ashara / Felwood.

author: peter_hammer
content:
So, what resto really needs is an option to make a choice based on current situation. This choice, whether good or bad, should either reward the shaman by better healing or be a waste of mana.

Since CH is already 99% (I checked some Kara40 logs) of the healing output, it should be treated as a default choice, CH spam bearing little or no negative consequences.

We, I think, **don't need another heal** because the existing ones are underused.

We should consider resto shaman's core identity and the class fantasy:

Identity: raid healing, smart heals, linking heals, no hots, lots of overheal, totems.
Class fantasy: healing waters, ancestral healing\guidance, shamanistic far sight.

**Option one: Overheal & Far Sight**
Talented CD that lets your healing waves temporarily add it's overheal to their target's health (with a coefficient), the health is added to targets after the primary effect wears off. When overheal is done, shaman gets some sort of healing debuff: % based healing reduction, negative spell haste, temporary lockout on heals, etc.

How it can look 
**Ancestral Vigour**:  *Overhealing done by your Healing Wave will increase total health of it's target by X% of overhealing done after Y seconds, but you will suffer a [Debuff] afterwards for Z seconds. Lasts Y seconds.*

**Option Two: Mana Spring and Healing Stream**

LHW and HW should apply some sort of effect that makes those two totems actually useful. HW can cause an overflow, increasing totem's effect on target for a few seconds, LHW could spread the totem's effect outside your group (doesn't stack with other shaman's MS and HS). There could be other options, I have no concrete ideas here.

**Option Three: Stacks.**

Make HW and LHW give you stacks (different kinds) that are consumed the next time you cast CH.
LHW stacks could make CH jump to one more target, while HW stacks could reduce CH cost or give it extra crit chance. If HW stacks are aquired by HW crits they could make next CH a guaranteed Crit.

author: Klarmeister
content:
Ok, now hear me out: I've run 4 60s sims on the new Ele Talents.

Deep Ele with only Lightning Bolt and Chain Lightning as a basline.

Deep Ele with chain lightning off CD, LB spam and every 6th cast molten blast to refresh flame shock for maximum effect on the refresh talent.
That rotation is really tight. If molten blast has the typical travel speed (34 yard/s), it barely works on max range.
Any pushback and you're fucked, especially because you lose your snapshot of Elemental Mastery (+CD-Trinket) on flame shock.
That being said, it's about a 7,5% damage increase compared to baseline.

Flame Spellhance (23/23/5) with molten blast spam is about a 3,5% damage increase, which is nice. It's also a 1 button rotation, so lot easier to play and basically gets no punishment for movement or cast-pushback. Which is very very nice and might make it on par to deep ele on many encounters. Also it has huge aoe potential.

And finally I simmed this monstrosity: https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/calculator?t0=Y0SqbAM89a&t1=sGD9my0at0&t2=xJEI6lz_0l&points=CoAYIqIDBCAY-FAEaALAQD-
The rotation is pretty easy: 
CL -> MB -> LB -> MB repeat.
With this modification you still get your flame shock ticks. It sims to about a 9% damage increase compared to baseline which makes it the strongest of the three (four) builds.

So, for resto following icyveins/wowhead (or any other classic) guides on preraid bis is bad because back in classic one of the main problems new resto shamans faced was poor mana economy.
This is not true on Turtle: you have water shield mana regen, BoW from paladins and hyjal teas that cost 20s a piece.
Instead of stacking as much mp5 as possible you should focus on getting more +healing, crit and haste.

author: Greybull-Ambershire
content:
# Shaman Leveling & Pre-BiS Guide

Firstly, I **highly recommend** checking out my post on the forums (https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=21611) as it's a much more complete/updated version of this pinned guide. It includes more complete Pre-BiS and consumables suggestions. It's also much longer though, so for a slightly more TL;DR version, stick to the one below.

I wrote this out as my personal levelling plan after compiling a lot of different tips from discussions in this channel. Since I noticed a lot of people asking for one, I'll share this in case it helps anyone save time by not having to research the same stuff. I'll be editing this if I come across any more relevant info, and I'd be grateful for any corrections or additions that anyone is willing to make. 

Big thanks to the following contributors who provided most of the knowledge compiled here: @Squid, @Zhafu, @Rinzu, @peter_hammer, @DemonBoyJr (Tel’Abim-Horde), @Bezawit, @Akos, @Not Normal, @poto, @Haaxor1689, @Zaaparou and more (sorry if I forgot any).

author: Greybull-Ambershire
content:
_ _
**[Race]**
- Troll is the best min-max race (quasi-Bloodlust haste racial for PvE and hex for PvP)
- Tauren is the most tanky for leveling (+5% hp, nature resist), has stomp for PvP + plainsrunning (biggest QoL racial in the game - saves us 2 talents on imp Ghost Wolf as well)
- Orc is still a decent choice for enhance PvE (axe skill helps, Blood Fury)

**[Gear & Stat Prios]**
- A shield with high armor is a always a top prio for tanking, eg. Compendium of the Fallen quest reward -> SM Cath shield -> Gilneas shield / Mara goblin shield / SWV shield
- Stats for tanking while leveling: +stam > +agi > +str > +int (when tanking at 60, +str becomes 2nd most important and +agi third)
- For healing: +int = +hp
- For DPS: +str = +agi > +stam > +int (+str & +agi roughly on par, at 60 +str is more valuable than +agi once you have consistent Flurry uptime, and your shocks scale with AP, but for raiding you still want to get 30%-35% crit before you start prioing +str)
- Stat prios thread: https://forum.turtle-wow.org/viewtopic.php?t=21159

author: Greybull-Ambershire
content:
_ _
**[Talents & Rotation]**

With this build, you can fill any role in dungeons: tank, DPS or heal (with some +int gear). Even if you solely want to DPS, this is arguably still the best build because you do practically the same DPS (the difference is really negligible) + have the benefit of being more tanky. If you want to skip tank talents, you could swap out Shield Spec. for Ancestral Knowledge. 

// To level 33
- 24p in enh: 5/5 Shield Spec > 2/2 Totemic Alignment > 3/3 Stable Shields > 3/3 Ancestral Guardian (before LS for mitigation) > Lightning Strike (take before AG if threat is a problem) > 1/5 Thundering Strikes > 2/2 Spirit Armor > 4/5 Thundering Strikes > 3/3 Elemental Weapons (first if feeling squishy) > Stormstrike (first if want more threat): https://talents.turtle-wow.org/shaman?points=-AoUYALAQDI-
- Rotation: Rockbiter + Lightning Shield, using Lightning Strike -> Storm Strike -> Earth Shock -> Lightning Strike. Maybe Searing if you can get value in same location
- Weapon: until Lightning Strike, a high dps dagger is just as good as a slow 2H; after Lightning Strike, a slow 2H is best
- At level 28,  get Compendium of the Fallen Q in TB and do SM: Lib for the shield
- At level 33, get the Jewelcrafting +stam trinkets

// Level 34-44
- 11p in ele to get to Clearcasting: 5/5 Convection > 2/5 Concussion (since few mobs do elemental dmg) OR 2/3 Elemental Warding (for mitigation in Maraudon) > 3/3 Elemental Devastation > Elemental Focus (Clearcasting!): https://talents.turtle-wow.org/shaman?points=FQAYI-AoUYALAQDI- OR https://talents.turtle-wow.org/shaman?points=FACYI-AoUYALAQDI-
- As a Tauren, at level 40, get Plainsrunning: head to the 2nd village you visit in Mulgore when you make a Tauren. The mount trainer there provides you a quest that leads to STV

// Level 44-50
- 6p in enh: 5/5 Thundering Strikes > 5/5 Element's Grace (raises threat w/o necessarily spending mana): https://talents.turtle-wow.org/shaman?points=FQAYI-AoVYALAQDIAo- OR https://talents.turtle-wow.org/shaman?points=FACYI-AoVYALAQDIAo-
- Rotation: after getting Elemental Focus at level 44, Frostbrand + Water Shield  (possibly with Stormwrought Totem for AoE), using Frost Shock -> Stormstrike -> Lightning Strike
- Optional: between 44-48, try to farm Earth Elementals in Badlands + occasional Uldaman runs

// Level 51-60
- I'm planning to go resto at 60, so I'll re-/dual spec here to farm pre-BiS early. Rush Imp Water Shield + Stable Shields, so like this: https://talents.turtle-wow.org/shaman?points=-FAAY-FoDoYIEYQC

author: Greybull-Ambershire
content:
_ _
**[Tanking Rotation]**
- Goal: to save mana, never generate more threat than needed to maintain aggro. So whenever possible, skip using the rotation below and just do auto-attacks + taunt. Or downrank your shocks when you don't need to go all out
- Imbue Rockbiter on a 1H and use a shield
- Mark your targets; the party should be focusing on your kill order to not split your threat thin
- Always ask for Judgment of Wisdom on the skull if there's a pala in the party to help with mana 
- With >=2 DPS in the party, placing down a Windfury Totem is justified. Especially if they are higher level or well-geared. Just tell them if they rip threat, they tank that mob as a deal. With a pala, Blessing of Salvation (-30% threat generation) can also be placed on the melee DPS in exchange for Windfury
- You can use Lightning Shield for the pull for added threat, switch to Water Shield halfway through and switch back to Lightning Shield whenever Clearcasting procs
- Pull with rank 1 Lightning Bolt (big range, basically 0 mana) + Chain Lightning (to establish max initial threat). For real max threat, optionally add a Molten Blast after as it has a short cast time which you can fit in the time the mobs run to you
- Running in, you'll want to Stormstrike on target 1, tab switch to Earth Shock target 2, and Lightning Strike target 3. If a target resists nature damage, use Frost Shock instead of Earth Shock
- Tab switch between targets giving each of them an Earth Shock and melee auto attack. When in doubt, place a Stoneclaw Totem, but it might be overdoing it
- AoE threat for >3 mobs: Stoneclaw Totem, or fire totems - Nova and Magma. If targets resist fire damage, Stoneclaw is your only AoE threat
- Oh shit: if a pull was bigger than anticipated or to quickly get aggro off healers: Fire Nova - huge snap threat, but mana intensive
- When a mob gets loose or runs towards a sheeped target, use max rank Lightning Bolt for high threat or Earth Shock for big snap threat
- After a pack is almost dead, move to a new one and Earth Shock one of those mobs to bring in that next pack
- To kite melee mobs & nuke them with casters before they arrive, use Chain Lightning to pull and Earthbind Totem to snare them. Optionally Frost Shock to help kite. Earthbind also works as an "oh shit" button to help a healer catch up
- For Caverns of Time: Black Morass, bring a Druid or Warlock to help CC the mobs (this dungeon eats every tank)

**[Healing Rotation]**
- No imbue
- Put down totems that are most beneficial for your group: Windfury, Strength of Earth, Flametongue and Mana Spring. Situationally, use poison/disease cleansing, Fire Resistance or even Healing Stream totems. 
- To keep your tank up in dungeons, use the latest rank of Healing Wave and Lesser Healing Wave, and -2 downranked Healing Wave, eg. r5 HW and LHW + r3 HW
- Chain Heal occasionally if there's lots of cleave dmg on the party
- Once you're raiding, all you really need is Chain Heal rank 1 besides dropping totems within range of your group. Besides that, you can throw out Spirit Link on tanks during enrage phases, eg. use on Maexxna before web wrap.

**[Totem Use While Solo]**
- They're not often worth dropping since you’ll be killing faster than the mana is worth to drop them (the mana cast is balanced around your whole party benefiting)
- That said, Earthbind weaving with a Swing timer is worth doing if you care about reducing the damage you take fighting mobs 1v1
- After getting Clearcasting, you can use Searing Totem + Stoneskin occasionally, mainly when it‘s possible to chain pull multiple mobs to the same spot

**[Earthbind Weaving/Kiting]**
- Earthbind Totem > Searing Totem > Flame Shock
- Melee, side strafe through them (don't expose your back) to get out of their range while your auto attack is resetting
- As your swing timer is resetting, position to re-enter the mobs' hitbox and swing again
- Re-apply Flame Shock / Lightning shield if efficient

author: Greybull-Ambershire
content:
_ _
**[Profs]**
- Herb/Alch, or Skin/LW for Stormshroud at ~50
- At ~53 drop LW for Herb to beef up your gold farming
- At 60, Herb for farming & Engi for raiding

**[Spells to Buy]**
- You can skip all but 1st rank of Resurrection
- Can technically skip Flametongue imbue
- Totems: you likely won't use the nature/frost/fire resistance totems during leveling enough to justify getting those. If you want, you can probably skip all totems besides the Poison/Disease cleansing totems, though for tanking you might want the strength/agi/WF totems. Water totems are optional (pretty weak while leveling but can be nice)
- If you don't plan to tank or play ele, skip the ranged damage spells (but never shocks)
- Everything else you need no matter the spec

**[Pre-BiS]**
- Enh: Focus on +stam and armor gear, ignoring defense beyond 15 (with the caveat that you'll still want defense, agility or direct dodge stats when it doesn't compromise stamina or armor to grab it). Take a look at Blacksmithing for the Hateforge set (https://database.turtle-wow.org/?itemset=615) and Towerforge: https://database.turtle-wow.org/?itemset=630. Also check out this thread for a general idea: https://forum.turtle-wow.org/viewtopic.php?t=20825. Later on, follow this explanation for any build trying to get crush/crit immune (= reaching 440 defense) https://wowwiki-archive.fandom.com/wiki/Attack_table
- Resto: Get as much +healing and +int as you can. Just do all the high level dungeons a few times and you should be good, eg. get the legs from DM West, decent options from BRD are the gloves from either Emperor or Moira/Mantle of Lost Hope/Soot Encrusted Footwear/Guiding Stave of Wisdom/Second Wind, Rivendare's Robe from Stratholme UD, Royal Seal of Eldre'Thalas from Dire Maul. Enchants to get for resto besides the typically recommended ones outside of T-WoW are enchanted armor kits that give +9 spell power. 2% haste to shoulder enchant, and then 1% haste vs +12 spellpower to helm/legs; ring/neck enchants (+12 healing) from JC. Belt buckle for +10 intellect
- Ele: basically need 15% hit on spells, as much int and crit as possible and spd, hit > crit > spd > int. If you have some gold there are two pairs of crafted cloth gloves that are really good, one with crit and one with haste. T1 belt/wrist from AH. The blue crafted Bloodvine set but don’t spend to much gold on stuff you can replace from Kara10. 2% crit quest reward trinket and DM trinket. It won’t be hard to get Onyxia group fairly fast, then you can get the Horde head and a good ring. UBRS has two trinkets and a great cloth head. Gloves of Unwinding Mystery
- You could look at a Classic BiS list and use Atlasloot to check the new dungeons like Kara Crypts (eg. Crown of Shattering, and BiS mace: Boneshatter Maul), Black Morass (eg. a very good mp5 totem), Hateforge Quarry (the Corrosive Core trinket is good if you lack +hit) and Stormwind Vaults (eg. Whip of Encouragement, haste is better if you're hit capped), and see if anything is an upgrade
- https://discord.com/channels/466622455805378571/810850759658831903/1410370767656587284

**[Macros]**
- https://github.com/Meridaw/Vanilla-Macros/tree/master/Shaman
- https://forum.turtle-wow.org/viewtopic.php?t=20390&sid=e49005ee5c14ebb030090e13b1a3c66f
- Place all totems:
/cast Windfury Totem
/cast Strength of Earth Totem
/cast Flametongue Totem
/cast Mana Spring Totem
/cast Water Shield
- With Call of Elements addon: new slot under keybinds + /coe for set up

**[Weapon Imbues & Shields]**
- Rockbiter + Lightning Shield until level 41/42 
- Then Frostbrand becomes better with Elemental Focus + Elemental Weapons talents
- At 60 you’re gonna use Windfury imbue, but you’re still gonna drop Windfury Totem (and Flametongue Totem) for your party even if you don’t benefit from it

**[Weapons]**
- Until you get the Lightning Strike talent, a high-DPS dagger is just as good as a slow 2H
- After getting Lightning Strike, try to have as slow of a 2H as possible.

author: DemonBoyJr (Tel’Abim-Horde)
content: You go into melee because Stormstrike increases your Earthshock damage by 20% and Lightning Strike+Lightning Shield actually provides decent melee damage as well since you’re already in melee. You actually sort of weave. Go in get your Storm/Lightning Strikes off, while backing off while they’re on CD to reduce melee damage a bit. Your white hits aren’t very strong so it’s best not to trade autos with actual melee specs. Gear is just like any Ele would gear for PvP, just make sure to wear a Shield since it provides a big chunk of your armor. Technically vs casters you can swap to a 2H like Maul of the Redeemer since the Shield armor won’t matter vs them. If you don’t like switching 1h(SP)+shield is always a safe bet.

author: DemonBoyJr (Tel’Abim-Horde)
content:
Earth Shock scales much better with SP than it does with AP and Ele gear will have more options for Spell Crit. Really the build wants to take advantage of the +100% crit damage  bonus modifier from Ele Fury talent. Point of the build is you’re much Tankier because you don’t sacrifice any damage using a 1H+Shield vs a 2H as Enhance, can take advantage of all the +armor talents, and can abuse damage reduction from Rockbiter while Emhance would use WF. Really though it’s just an alternative and flexible playstyle for people who have geared as Ele since ultimately you’re gonna use the best gear you’ve gotten from raids. Not everyone is full kitted out in Naxx+ gear for both Ele and Enh. Just a shift a damage from White damage WF procs to more Spell Damage.

author: sailorVEVO
content:
@arrolla 

Caster-Healer hybrid Ele Levelling
This build is oriented around the Fire suite of Elemental Shaman spells. I also take points in Nature (Lightning) spells and use either based on gearing.

10 - 24
Convection, Elemental Warding, 2x Concussion, Elemental Focus, Improved Molten Blast, 2x Call of Thunder
25-33
Call of Flame, 2x Call of Thunder, Elemental Mastery, Elemental Fury, 1x Call of Thunder, 1x Improved Fire Totems
34-40
Lightning Mastery, Earthquake

This finishes up our points in Elemental. At this point, Nature DMG is best for AoE and Fire DMG is best for single-target/solo. Use them based on targets, party comp, and whatever type of gear you have (Nature SP vs Fire SP) You can choose to go down into Enhancement for more mitigation and melee dps, or you can go into Restoration for support. We'll go with restoration for this guide.
41-50
Improved Healing Wave, Tidal Mastery or Tidal Focus (Mastery if you prefer Nature spells, focus if you prefer Fire spells or Healing efficiency)
51-60
Totemic Mastery, Healing Focus, 5x Tidal Mastery or Tidal Focus (Choose the other you didn't pick), 2x Nature's Grace

This isn't the perfect, most optimal levelling talents, but I've gone with this route a few times when doing an Ele/Resto playstyle and it felt VERY smooth. Just focus INT gear and grab Spell Power or Spell Damage pieces where you can, Healing Power also doesn't hurt.  Once you hit 60, respec to Resto and begin gearing!

author: DemonBoyJr (Tel’Abim-Horde)
content:
https://youtu.be/o90HvELvCpA?si=_SW9P8R0vyAc9nj9

Video courtesy of Zapp

You basically pull as many packs as you can comfortably given your HP pool; I do 4 packs, but for new players I recommend 1-2 packs. Put on Earth Shield and have Flametongue weapon imbue for +30% fire totem damage. Drop Stoneskin/Grace of Air totems to reduce damage/increase dodge. Open with Fire Nova Totem, after it explodes drop Magma Totem and finish them with Nova Totem. I personally wait until there’s 6 sec left on Magma Totem, i’ve done 8 sec left, but sometimes they’re left with a smidge of HP. You’ll use a 1h+Shield.

https://talents.turtle-wow.org/shaman?points=FYAYLAQDBC-EoQYALAQT-AY

here’s an example build. Main thing is you want your Totems to do as much damage as possible while also being as Tanky as you can. At fresh 60 with some blues you can probably pretty comfortably do 2 pack pulls once you know what you’re doing. No point in doing 3 pack pulls since it doesn’t really save time, so just do 2 pack pulls until you feel comfortable enough to do 4 packs pulls.

author: Squid
content:
From everything I have tested, they still seems to proc at a normal rate. HoJ and Windfury can proc together. What I think has confused a lot of people is a combination of two things. 

1. Windfury attacks cannot proc HoJ attacks and vice versa. They happen simultaneously off the same base attack, but the extra attacks can never chain each other.

2. Addons like DPSmate treat these extra attacks the same as a normal auto attack. So when you count the number of total auto attacks to actual procs, the proc rate suffers. This I think is basically just a visual thing, because not all of those attacks have a chance to actually proc anything. 

So when I have compared the number of actual attacks that have a chance to proc these effects with the actual proc rate, everything has seemed fine to me. Hope this is a fairly clear explanation of how windfury and other extra attack effects work and where the confusion seems to come from.

author: Kairion
content:
Talent tree suggestions are a bit a touchy subject with the upcoming changes ita not entirely clear what will be best. Generally speaking elemental/enhancement mixes are better than enh + resto talents. Shamans want to end fights quickly. An instant heal is nice but you need the help with mana from elemental focus too much. I recommend 30pts minimum in enhancement. Elements grace is a very powerful talent

If you fight a class hat relies more on physical damage than you (Warrior, Ret-Paladin, Feral Druid, non-assasin variants of rogue or Hunters) strongly consider using a shield. But the specifics depend a lot on your gear vs their gear.

Stamina, 5% hitchance in total for physical hits are a must.
Grab pieces with the most combined agi, strength & stamina. If its more crit or more ap doesnt matter much. You want the biggest pile of stats in total. DO NOT grab leather unless your chainmail options are awful. Armor matters for the physical matchups.

 Dodge, block parry & defense are largely irrelevant for pvp.

author: Temu
content: NS was nerfed in the latest patch to spells being cast at 75% power instead of the original 100%. Presumably this was for pvp reasons, which means devs sought to promote the newly introduced EQ spell in the Ele tree. However, with the simultaneous dmg dampening in pvp, NS got hit double - the dmg output from an NS spell is now 0.75x0.8=0.6=60% dmg of the spell being cast. This weakens the utility of NS significantly. Ele/resto, the OG pvp spec has been consistently hit by nerfs since the first iteration of CC2. It did not need this. It seems to me that devs try to force experimenting with alternative specs onto players just to promote their own ideas for the class. Please reverse NS to its original power and let those who wish to play shamans as a pure caster/supporter class in pvp do so.

author: Greybull-Ambershire
content:
Ele idk, but full T2 should be best for enhancement. I've asked around about resto bis, got a lot of input from @Not Normal and the TLDR was that 5/8 T2 is pretty dogshit, but there's a case for [3/8 T2](https://tinyurl.com/3pieceTier2), especially if you already have T2 head/legs:
-# - T2 bracers are technically bis - Loomguard Armbraces are virtually as good, just missing some mp5 and a bit of int
-# - T2 chest isn't gonna be technically bis, Robes of the Exalted or Red Dragonscale chest are both better in terms of raw throughput (it's a tossup between these - just depends if you like the stam or 5 int & +2 healing)
-# - T2 boots approach Pure Thought, but Pure Thought should drop like candy and are better anyway

So with head/legs, bracers are your best 3/8 pick. But given how highly contested T2 will be, you might as well not chase T2 set bonus and just grab what pieces individually have good stats. [This](https://tinyurl.com/RawBiS) would be your bis for raw throughput. It'd also help general guild gearing by easing T2 comp. Ofc you can use your T2 helm, but if you're open minded, Crown of Molten ascension is actually better despite being a dps item just because haste is cracked. It's advisable to ditch T2 with this setup though, the easy to grab K10 legs would be like +25 healing power worth of value higher

content:
full threat gear will be 3.5 enh 5/5, t3 bracer, gloves, belt and ring, Nelth’s or Scaleshield with Seal of the Damned to cap out on spellhit when elemental devastation and emerald blessing is active, Sadist’s Collar for beautiful mix of stam, crit and AP, Chain-Cloak of the Rookguard for obvious reasons, Thunderfall… because… Thunderfall. Natural Alignment crystal for your active trinket slot and Heart of Dreams for your passive trinket slot.

For mit it will still be full 2.5 with Mark of C’thun or Pendant of Purified Demon’s Blood, still Chain-Cloak lol, Bands of the Surgebreaker, Vek’lor Gloves or Rune Infused Gauntlets, Stoneslate Belt, Thick Qirajihide Belt or Therazane’s Link, some combination of Archimtiros Ring, Bronze Dragonflight tank ring and Vek’lor ring, King’s Edict and Araxxna’s Husk for double passive mit trinkets, Styleen’s is ok too. Wear Zandalarian Hero Badge if you know there’s a big enrage phase later in the fight - if not, pop it before combat and swap it for another trinket - you will keep the buff. Forgotten Raven’s Mallet and Bulwark of Enduring Earth for the bulkiest weapon/shield combo of course.

For aoe shenanigans, Totem of Tides with Sigil of Ancient Accord and Grail of Forgotten Memories is pretty cool. Bonus points if you have a bracer and pair of boots enchanted with vampirism. It’s pretty good sustain lol

For threat enchants- ZG on head/leg, might of the scourge on shoulder, stats on chest and jewellery, crusader on weapon, str on bracer, threat on gloves, str on belt, SP on boots.

For mit enchants- 100 HP or 2% dodge on head/leg, fortitude of the scourge on shoulder, stam on jewellery, bracer, boots, shield. 100 HP on chest. 15 agi on weapon and gloves. 5 def on belt. 1% dodge on cape or 70 armor if you’e poor.

TLDR Stat prio/value per point-
threat: hitcap>crit(melee or spell)>str>sp>agi>ap>int
mit: stam>parry>dodge>defense>agi>armor

author: Doite
content:
Correct an as below states.
* Mages: In TWOW you can only sheep 2x healers. Dont try more, so allocate these, be clear for other mages not to sheep. Sheep the 2 healers closest to boss is usually most simple.
* Hunter: Turn off salvation, take inner warrior closest to boss - aimed shot, run away. Call out when dies.
* Tanks: 1x Tank holds boss. People underestimate this, but I rarely see a tank that tanks this correctly. Boss should be tanked exactly where he stands, and facing exactly towards the raid. Tank should stand in slope infront and reposition him over and over agian. Reason for the importance, is that he will when teleported run towards healers, which will stand in a straightline - so you want to be able to pick up as he runs so he never reaches. Then 1-2 tanks on 1 side each where of the raid. Warriors cleve.
* Kill order: Unsheeped healers > Broken healers unable to be resheped > Warriors.
* Timer: Set to 20 sec pulltimer. When 3 seconds lefts hunter should start casting aimed shot (so its out at 0) and at 1.5 sec left mages should start sheeping (so its out at 0).

Have fun.

author: Dwi
content:
in the absence of one, mostly behave like a ranged DPS but learn to make the best use of your insane support kit too

stay with the casters, except after two minutes when you have to go within an earth shock's range of the boss to drop totems so they can affect the melees in your group. Cast earth shock while walking whenever you got to run away from meteor showers and shit and can't cast. Cast earth shock too when you notice some monster spell such as healing or shadow volley can be interrupted. Use a proper resistance totem for fights when there is one. Sometimes it's just obvious  (big fire guy that radiates fire inside a volcano), or sometimes the guild leader will tell everyone to use Greater Fire Protection Potion and that's your clue. Cast/recast poison or disease cleansing totems as soon as people in your party get these debuffs. Finally and maybe the one that's easy to forget but very troublesome: have your tremor totem ON for fights that involve Fear. You'll memorize which bosses soon enough, if the raidcaller doesn't have the habit to remind shamans to use tremor. If the BigWigs addon starts a countdown for a Fear, like in the Magmadar fight, get a little closer (if needed) and cast Tremor about 5.5 seconds before that fear happens. Tremor pulses every 6 seconds (the time of one D&D turn) and this will make people in your party get almost instantly un-feared and they think you're a god if you do that

author: Dwi
content:
It's way more comfortable here than in vanilla:

- Totems don't use your global cooldown (you're just locked out of the same element totems for 1.5, you can cast any other skill or even cast 4 totems at once). This allows for cleansing, tremor, general adaptability to be weaved in mid rotation without taking a second
- 'totem swap' DOESN'T exist here. Windfury is an aura so it stops working immediately if you cast Grace of Air. You'll need less mana to support your melees
- clearcasting talent is doubled, meaning crit effectively becomes your mana stat instead of mp5.
- a lot of pre-raid bis options in the custom content (dungeons, professions etc) meaning you won't have to cast level 4 bolts in early raiding
- tier sets actually exists for us now too. No more using bloodvine set or naxx trash
- we have a fire alternative rotation too

author: Svargth
content:
Well, we’ve already spent hours testing since the patch was implemented. I personally play on Tel'Abim (PvP) and I regularly play only three healer characters: a Resto Shaman, a Holy Priest, and a Resto Druid. I’ve been raiding MC, BWL, AQ20 and AQ40, and Naxx for a full year now, so I know what I’m talking about.

Yesterday we ran MC with the guild. As a Resto Shaman, I usually place 1st or 2nd on almost every kill. Yesterday, the three priests in the guild—who usually ranked well below me in the logs—outperformed me in healing in almost every fight.

author: Svargth
content:
Not only are Holy Priest single-target heals stronger, but now Lightwell also lets them perform a kind of mini Chain Heal for 10 casts. On top of that, they can heal better than Chain Heal because Prayer of Healing is no longer limited to the priest’s own group—it can now be cast on any raid group.

And… wait, there’s more! They can recover 30% of their mana if each heal they cast is different from the previous one. And if that weren’t enough, the Ascendance talent is amazing…

So they’re better at single-target healing, and now they also have more tools than just a simple Chain Heal to heal the raid without it causing a massive mana loss. Prayer of Healing Rank 1, with 900 healing spell power, heals for around 800 health on average (non-crit) to the whole group, and if the priest manages a proper rotation, they can recover 30% of the mana spent.

author: Svargth
content: Ascendance completely blows Spirit Link out of the water.

author: trallnar
content:
I'm leveling a tank shaman now, so i just went through that.

At level 26 you get Water Shield and Mana Stream totem, which help a LOT. 

When tanking, I usually use a down-ranked earth shock instead of max rank. Its good enough for threat.

At level 33, if you are really lucky the "totem of the tides" from the Stormwrought dungeon makes your water shield constantly proc for aoe damage and threat. It really helps a lot with holding threat while leaving on water shield instead of swapping water/lightning shields. (And lightning shield is mana intensive, so taking it off the simple rotation helps a lot)

author: trallnar

author: trallnar
content:
Don't spend all your mana 😅

Mark the first kill target with skull so dps has to target the main one.

Pull with rank 1 lightning bolt and LOS to group up ranged enemies, using fire nova and stoneclaw totem for aoe threat.

Once you've established threat on the main target, as long as your dps don't focus others you should have enough threat by the time target 1 dies. You can conserve mana and not spam lightning strike or earth shock. Magma totem is a huge mana drain.

author: Zeruel
content:
2h + Wf is significantly weaker in pvp than in a raid because of all the raid buff and consumes AP you're typically not getting. (WF basically is a big multiplier on your melee stats. If you don't have a lot of those stats then wf isn't doing that much)

And while supposedly we're "OP" at high-end gear levels like Naxx and k40,  it doesn't feel that way for my own experience at the MC and BWL gear level on amber.

I often go rockbiter instead of WF if I want to get kills. Because it's a huge boost to my AP and it also boosts empowered Lightning Shield procs and boosts Earth Shock while wf doesnt. And the little shield is kinda nice too i guess

But at the end of the day I don't think physhance 2h is the way to go right now on amber or prior to naxx and kara40. It feels squishy and feels like it can be hard to secure kills before you yourself die. Beyond that I can't tell you what you *should* be doing, someone else will need to chime in there
